I don't like sand.
https://tenor.com/view/ahh-noo-darth-vader-sand-gif-16141824

There's nothing outright wrong with this, but I'm against [Zeno resolutions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zeno's_paradoxes) on principle. A resolution should be, at least in some way, tailored to the subject it's covering. Replace "industrial sand mining" with whatever and nothing would change

Why just sand mining? Why not fracking, or oil drilling, or fishing, or chemical fertilizer use? This is the positive legislation version of a natsov template repeal where Banana brags about not even reading the target to make a point
Changed the channel name: [Next] GA - Sand Industry Standards Act
This point has convinced me
While I have nothing against narrow resolutions, there ought to be some compelling reason to be addressing the narrow topic rather than a broad one. Otherwise you're just micromanaging.
Cretox Luther nailing his 95 GA theses to the door
Others include “Citing Trends is Make-Believe” and “Putting the Cart Before the Sausage”
Is "Citing Trends is Make-Believe" things like Simone saying microcredit is going out of style?
Which like, even if it might be true in real life, no reason to assume that NS operates the same
Exactly
“Acknowledging that such and such programs are PROVEN to be ineffective…”
“Concerned about the harmful impacts of program IN MANY COUNTRIES”
It’s “many nations are saying, believe me, believe me”
"Drug criminalization doesn't work"?
Establish a logical connection instead of declaring things to Be True
Okay now what's "Putting the cart before the sausage"?
Basing resolutions on what RL laws do without understanding why the RL law ended up that way
You see it a lot with labor resolutions that weirdly cripple labor because they’re based on RL laws that do it due to political compromises that don’t exist in the GA
Even that’s better than the “drug criminalization has been harmful in many countries” that Simone would write
Actually, he’s probably write it specifically about e-cigs or something lol
